questions.question: Which spelling is British English?
questions.explanation: British English uses "colour", "centre" and "organise", while American English uses "color", "center" and "organize".

questions.question: What is the American English word for the British "lorry"?
questions.explanation: British "lorry" = American "truck". Similarly: lift/elevator, flat/apartment, biscuit/cookie.

questions.question: What is the difference between a dialect and an accent?
options: A dialect includes vocabulary and grammar; an accent is only about pronunciation
An accent includes grammar; a dialect is only pronunciation
They are exactly the same thing
questions.explanation: An accent refers only to pronunciation, while a dialect also includes differences in vocabulary and grammar.

questions.question: What is "Singlish"?
options: Singaporean English, mixing English with Mandarin, Malay and Tamil
questions.explanation: Singlish is Singaporean English, a variety blending English with Mandarin, Malay and Tamil influences.

questions.question: Is one variety of English more "correct" than the others?
options: No - all varieties are valid, but standard forms are expected in formal writing
Yes - only British English is correct
Yes - only American English is correct
Yes - Australian English is the world standard
questions.explanation: No variety is inherently more correct. All are valid language systems, though school and formal writing usually expect a consistent standard variety.
